title: Maintenance System — Flight Deck — Installation of the Central Maintenance Display Unit
abstract: Installation of a fixed maintenance system display at the third occupant station, replacing the portable terminal connection that line stations found slow and awkward on a turnaround.

sections.planning_reason: Early operators found that reading the central maintenance system through a portable terminal was slow on a turnaround and that the flight deck connection was awkward to reach with the third occupant seat stowed. Six operators asked for a permanently installed screen within the first two years of service. The request was accepted as a customer-driven standard change; there is no defect and no airworthiness driver.
sections.description: A fixed display unit is installed at the third occupant station, fed from the existing maintenance system bus with no new processing. The unit sits in a bracket that picks up existing panel hard points and the aperture is protected with silicone edging. The portable terminal connection remains available and can be used in parallel.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make the aircraft electrically safe and stow the third occupant seat. Remove the panel at the third occupant station in zone 241 and cut the display aperture to the template supplied with the kit. Deburr the aperture and fit the silicone edging AES4363-5C. Install the display bracket on the existing hard points. Route the display feed from the maintenance system bus, working through the forward cabin in zone 226, and secure it clear of the seat track. Install the display unit D4520115601387 and connect it. Do the display power-up test and confirm that the maintenance system pages are readable in daylight and in night lighting. Confirm that the maintenance terminal display 626TM still functions in parallel. Refit the panel and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00303 that are pre MOD-164788. There is no operational or airworthiness driver: the display is a convenience for the line station and an operator that does not want it may leave the aircraft as delivered.
sections.material_note: Kit K4520-1015-01 contains the display unit, the bracket, the edging, the aperture template and the feed cable. Lead time is sixteen weeks. Nothing is returned to Aeralis.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience. There is no compliance date and no consequence to leaving this Service Bulletin unembodied.

title: Maintenance System — Flight Deck — Installation of the Central Maintenance Display Unit

issue.reason: Re-worded from an optional improvement to a prerequisite of the rack replacement bulletin, with a pointer to it and the consequence of skipping it stated.

abstract: Installation of a fixed maintenance system display at the third occupant station. Originally a convenience for the line station, this Service Bulletin is now the prerequisite step that gives an aircraft the flight deck aperture and the panel connectors the rack replacement bulletin terminates on.

sections.planning_reason: Early operators found that reading the central maintenance system through a portable terminal was slow on a turnaround and that the flight deck connection was awkward to reach with the third occupant seat stowed. Six operators asked for a permanently installed screen within the first two years of service, and the Service Bulletin was issued as a customer-driven option with no airworthiness driver. That framing is no longer the whole picture. The rack and concentrator standard introduced later reuses the aperture cut and the two panel connectors installed here, so an aircraft that skipped this Service Bulletin cannot take the later one without separate flight deck panel work at its own cost and lead time.
sections.description: A fixed display unit is installed at the third occupant station, fed from the existing maintenance system bus with no new processing. The unit sits in a bracket that picks up existing panel hard points and the aperture is protected with silicone edging. The portable terminal connection remains available and can be used in parallel.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make the aircraft electrically safe and stow the third occupant seat. Remove the panel at the third occupant station in zone 241 and cut the display aperture to the template supplied with the kit. Deburr the aperture and fit the silicone edging AES4363-5C. Install the display bracket on the existing hard points. Route the display feed from the maintenance system bus, working through the forward cabin in zone 226, and secure it clear of the seat track. Install the display unit D4520115601387 and connect it. Do the display power-up test and confirm that the maintenance system pages are readable in daylight and in night lighting. Confirm that the maintenance terminal display 626TM still functions in parallel. Refit the panel and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00303 that are pre MOD-164788. This Service Bulletin is a prerequisite of Service Bulletin MRD-45-1021 and must be embodied before it. An operator planning the rack and concentrator standard on an aircraft below the production cut-in should read this Service Bulletin as the first half of that work and not as an optional improvement that may be skipped: the later bulletin explicitly excludes aircraft that have not embodied it.
sections.material_note: Kit K4520-1015-01 contains the display unit, the bracket, the edging, the aperture template and the feed cable. Lead time is sixteen weeks. The display backlight used by this standard went out of production in 2021 and the display content of the kit is drawn from the residual pool, so an operator planning the rack standard should order both kits together rather than in sequence.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accomplishment of Service Bulletin MRD-45-1021 on the same aircraft. Otherwise at the operator's convenience.

revision_history.reason: Restated as a prerequisite of the rack and concentrator bulletin
